title: Pages, links and composition
description: How page files, links and section composition work. The element examples live on pages 1–6.

add_paragraph.text: Each element is documented in one place, and each appears **three times**: normal, left column and right column. This page covers the page itself, not the elements.

add_special_note.heading: Element pages
add_special_note.text: Text — page 1 · Media — page 2 · Cards and people — page 3 · Publications — page 4 · Data and actions — page 5 · Embeds and 3D — page 6.

add_paragraph.text: A page under `data/pages/` is a single flow or a list of sections. A standalone page has no numbered section head; the sticky bar carries its title.

content_of_rows_separated_by_comma: Overrides the title in the lead.
Optional; `text` runs prose in two columns.
Section ids or inline section objects.

add_paragraph.text: The same resolver is used in prose, cards, publications, buttons and notes.
A page can list section ids (`["about", "research"]`) or inline section objects. Each section keeps its own heading, intro and flow. A section file can be reused on several pages.

add_special_note.heading: Home sections
add_special_note.text: The home page reads `data/site.json` and renders the section ids in order. Only home sections show the numbered head.

add_special_note.heading: Variants
add_special_note.text: A normal copy has no `column`. Left and right copies share a row. If you add a `column` to something that is already full width, it moves into that lane; remove it and it returns to full width.
